summary: NO-SHIP: concurrent full resets violate the required clean-snapshot guarantee, and the destructive reset UI drops transport failures.
triage: review-gate SKILL.md § Triage governs: render EVERY finding as a full table row, never inside a dialog; then ask the ROUND before the rows — take every Proposed decision as it stands, or decide row by row — and `as proposed` ends the round in that ONE action; only if row-by-row was chosen, ask per finding with that row's Proposed decision as the first option, a reject or defer taking a free-text reason; echo back ONLY the rows that carried free text, and none if the round was decided by selection alone; max 2 rounds, append decisions.md and COMMIT it with this artifact.

findings.title: Spec fidelity: overlapping resets cancel the successful reset's clean snapshot
findings.body: Every reset increments `backupGeneration` and clears `backupScheduled`. A successful reset schedules its required clean snapshot, but when a second queued reset begins it invalidates that timer; if the second reset fails, `resumeBackupWrites({reschedule:false})` schedules nothing. Concurrent requests are reachable because both popup and tab surfaces expose the reset without global in-flight coalescing. The test comment at `src/runtime/background-bootstrap.test.ts:467-469` explicitly acknowledges the no-snapshot terminal state instead of asserting against it, contradicting `.scratch/scope-race-hardening/spec.md:123`.
findings.recommendation: Coalesce concurrent full resets or preserve a monotonic clean-snapshot obligation until fulfilled. Add a regression test where one reset succeeds, an overlapping reset fails, timers fire, and exactly one default-state snapshot is written.

findings.title: Full reset transport rejection bypasses all failure feedback
findings.body: After destructive confirmation, `resetEverything` directly awaits `onCommand` without catching rejection. The traced path `dispatchWithResult`/`sendCommand` also leaves `browser.runtime.sendMessage` rejection unhandled, although the parallel backup-mutation channel explicitly documents and settles service-worker replacement failures at `src/platform/stateStore.ts:173-191`. Consequently a reset request whose message round trip fails produces neither the localized error banner nor retry guidance, leaving the user unable to distinguish an unstarted request from an interrupted operation.
findings.recommendation: Catch command transport rejection and map it to the reset error banner while preserving retry confirmation. Add a test with a rejecting `onCommand` after confirmation.

next_steps: Fix and test overlapping successful/failed reset scheduling before merge.
